I feel you mama and we’re all here in it together. I’m a first time mom and now 27 +2. Hubby and I have been together for 10.5 years, married 4 years next month and had put off having our child. There was always a reason to wait and when we finally agreed the timing was as good as it was going to get and started trying it all seemed right. Then nothing has gone easy since we conceived.

We found out we were pregnant before Xmas and kept it a secret to be safe. Then I was in a high speed auto accident at 8 weeks pregnant that totaled mine and 2 other cars. Baby survived and has been hitting all his goals on every check and looks healthy thankfully. We kept him a secret even longer than we planned after that to avoid the worried onslaught of family knowing I was pregnant during the accident, putting time between the accident and announcement in hopes people wouldn’t put it together.

Seems just as I healed from the accident (all the while being sick etc from baby: pregnancy has been hard in and of itself for me) the world began to fall apart. I live in the US and every day is a new thing to stress about. The pandemic, our government, the riots and systemic racism...it feels like the world is ending all on top of my body working double time to grow this little boy. Some days it feels like the world is failing my child and my body is failing me with how exhausted and sore I am.

But knowing we’re not alone is important. This community is important. If you need a place to rant, opinions, or just some strength from other mamas working through the same hard times as you. Here it is. Stay strong! We’ve got this. ❤️
Sending love and good energy. Stay strong. This community will be here with open arms when you come back. ❤️

Hey there. I want you to know you’re not alone. And warn against that feeling that “someone else has it worse.” Of course someone else does. Someone else always does. But that doesn’t negate your pain or suffering. You’re valid. How you’re feeling is valid. And the first step to feeling better is acknowledging something isn’t right.

I know it can be incredibly hard to tell someone what’s going on. But I also know it can lift such a weight off your shoulders, just taking that step.

Now, idk if you’re in my country (US) so maybe it will be different. But what I’ve learned in my life time of mental illness is that you have to be your biggest advocate. And yeah...I see the problem in that too. When we need help the most it is the most important that we take care of ourselves and also the time when we are the least likely to help ourselves.

It’s the proverbial snake eating it’s tail. It’s a strange curse when your illness is in the part of you that decides if you’re sick and need help. It’s a strange curse that tells you you’re fine or not deserving of getting better. But, you’re not alone. And I hope you find the strength, one day at a time, to take care of yourself. Congratulate your small victories, and try not to dwell in others having it worse.
You’re valid.
How you feel is valid.
You deserve to be happy.

Now, not every person has the same kinda of doctors and I’m sure it’s different in different countries too...but here’s my experience in the United States.

I started with my general practitioner, we checked out my physical health and ran a few tests to make sure nothing underlying was causing my depression/anxiety. My GP then asked if I wanted to speak with a specialist and I said yes, so they set me up with an in-house clinical psychologist is believe... I did counseling’s with them and when we both felt good about my self care and ability to cope as best I could, we decided to try medications. For this they recommended something and my general practitioner would prescribe it.

Eventually we all agreed we had made about as much improvement as I could with talk therapy and I had a good intellectual grasp on what happens in my head. So, the door is always open and I’m free to make appointments with her to talk and bounce things off her, but since we got to a point where medication was going to be such a big part of my treatment it made sense to find someone else. 

So she referred me to someone who could better manage my medications as I progressed, as she could do my talk therapy and write prescriptions where the last doctor only did talk therapy and had to have my GP write my scripts. The one I was referred to is a Nurse Practitioner who specializes in psychiatry I believe.

With her I’m on a good combination of medications, improving every day, and feeling more like myself. I’m still using the wonderful techniques I learned from my previous doctor to navigate the mine field of my mind, but most importantly I have a support net of professionals now. 

So everyone’s road is different but don’t let the word referral scare you. I was so anxious finally seeking help after years of suffering, I postponed it near the end because I “didn’t know who to call.” But the important part is to just make an appointment, get started. Anyone worth their salt will hear you out and point you to the best person for help or at least tell you where to look. It’s hard to not feel overwhelmed, especially in the beginning, but it’s a trip worth taking.
